q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis: NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
Today is August 13, 2026. Q2 FY2027 earnings will be released in Q2 of fiscal 2027 (typically August-September 2026 timeframe based on NVIDIA's typical earnings calendar). This means the earnings release is likely within **2-4 weeks**, making this very near-term.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The research provides NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 guidance released on May 20, 2026: **$91.0 billion ±2%** for Q2 FY2027.

This is the forward guidance that was already provided. The question asks what guidance NVIDIA will give when it reports Q2 FY2027 results (which happens at the end of Q2). The resolution is asking for NVIDIA's NEW forward guidance for what comes next (presumably Q3 FY2027), not reiterating the Q2 guidance that was already announced.

However, re-reading more carefully: the question asks "What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release?" This is ambiguous but most naturally reads as: when NVIDIA releases its Q2 FY2027 earnings report, what forward guidance will they provide?

Given that we're currently at August 13, 2026, and Q2 FY2027 is the quarter ending August 2026, the earnings would be released very soon (likely this month or early September 2026). At that point, NVIDIA will provide guidance for Q3 FY2027.

NVIDIA has shown consistent guidance accuracy recently, and typically guides conservatively. The Q1 FY2027 guidance of $91.0B was described as "well above average estimates," suggesting NVIDIA is positioning conservatively but confidently.

**Most likely scenario**: NVIDIA will provide guidance in the range of **$95-105 billion** for Q3 FY2027 (the quarter they'll be guiding to from the Q2 earnings call), representing sequential growth consistent with their recent trajectory.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Deterioration in AI demand or slower data center spending
- Geopolitical restrictions impacting revenue (the research notes they exclude China compute revenue)
- Weaker-than-expected enterprise spending or IT budget constraints
- Competitive pressure or market share losses
- Supply chain or manufacturing constraints
- Macro economic slowdown affecting customer capex

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Accelerating AI infrastructure demand exceeding expectations
- New product launches or higher-margin products driving upside
- Enterprise adoption of generative AI expanding faster than modeled
- Potential relaxation of China trade restrictions (though currently not assumed)
- Strong cloud provider capex cycles
- International expansion driving incremental revenue
- Better-than-expected gross margins enabling higher volume/pricing

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides one critical data point: **NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 guidance was $91.0 billion ±2%** (released May 20, 2026).

No other historical guidance comparisons are provided in the research or background. However, this $91.0B guidance for Q2 is the most recent forward-looking guidance available and represents the market's current expectations. 

Typical NVIDIA quarterly guidance patterns show consistent sequential growth in strong periods. If Q2 came in near the $91B guidance and demand remains strong, Q3 guidance would likely show further growth of 3-10% sequentially, pointing to a range of $94-100B.

---

## Reasoning on the range provided: 99.5 to 115.5 billion

The range spans $99.5B to $115.5B. This is notably higher than the Q2 guidance of $91.0B that was already provided. This suggests the question is indeed asking about guidance for **Q3 FY2027 or later**, not the Q2 guidance that already exists.

Given:
- Q2 guidance: $91.0B
- The high end of the provided range ($115.5B) implies significant sequential growth
- Historical NVIDIA growth rates have been strong but typically 5-15% quarterly growth in good environments
- $91B × 1.10 = $100.1B (10% growth)
- $91B × 1.27 = $115.6B (27% growth - quite high for one quarter)

A 10-15% sequential growth from Q2 to Q3 would put guidance around **$100-105B**, which falls in the lower-to-middle portion of the provided range.

The upper end ($115B+) would require exceptional acceleration or possibly includes a full-year guidance reframing, which seems less likely unless there's a major positive catalyst.

**Most probable outcome**: Guidance clusters in the **$100-108 billion** range, representing healthy but not exceptional sequential growth.

q_45367.research_text: NVIDIA released its Q1 FY2027 earnings on May 20, 2026, and provided forward guidance for Q2 FY2027. The company expects revenue to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/). This guidance is well above the average quarterly revenue estimate of $86.84 billion, according to LSEG [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). NVIDIA's outlook explicitly does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/). Additionally, GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be 74.9% and 75.0% respectively, plus or minus 50 basis points [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/). Operating expenses are projected to be approximately $8.5 billion (GAAP) and $8.3 billion (non-GAAP) [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/).
